content: 1. Paclitaxel (protein-bound): Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of paclitaxel by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 2. Pacritinib: Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of pacritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Monitor closely if unavoidable. 3. Palbociclib: Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of palbociclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Paliperidone: Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of paliperidone via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 5. Palovarotene: Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of palovarotene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or reduce the palovarotene dose by 50% if unavoidable. Monitor closely. 6. Panobinostat: Erythromycin base and panobinostat both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Panobinostat prescribing information advises against combining with QT-prolonging drugs. 7. Pantothenic acid: Erythromycin base decreases the level or effect of pantothenic acid by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Parecoxib: Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of parecoxib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Paromomycin: Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of paromomycin via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Paroxetine: Erythromycin base and paroxetine both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 11. Pasireotide: Erythromycin base and pasireotide both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 12. Pazopanib: Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of pazopanib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or reduce the pazopanib dose to 400 mg/day if unavoidable. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. 13. Pemetrexed: Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of pemetrexed by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 14. Penicillin G aqueous: Erythromycin base decreases the effect of penicillin G aqueous due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance is unknown. 15. Penicillin VK: Erythromycin base decreases the effect of penicillin VK due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance is unknown. 16. Pentamidine: Erythromycin base and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. 17. Pentobarbital: Pentobarbital decreases the level or effect of erythromycin base by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 18. Perphenazine: Erythromycin base and perphenazine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 19. Pexidartinib: Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of pexidartinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or reduce the pexidartinib dose if unavoidable. Pexidartinib is associated with hepatotoxicity. 20. Phenindione: Erythromycin base increases the effect of phenindione by inhibiting its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 21. Phenobarbital: Phenobarbital decreases the level or effect of erythromycin base by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 22. Phenytoin: Phenytoin decreases the level or effect of erythromycin base by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 23. Pimozide: Erythromycin base increases the level of pimozide by inhibiting its metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. 24. Pioglitazone: Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of pioglitazone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Piperacillin: Erythromycin base decreases the effect of piperacillin due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Pitavastatin: Erythromycin base increases the toxicity of pitavastatin by inhibiting its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or limit the pitavastatin dose to 1 mg/day. 27. Pitolisant: Erythromycin base and pitolisant both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 28. Pomalidomide: Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of pomalidomide via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 29. Ponatinib: Ponatinib increases the level of erythromycin base via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Posaconazole: Erythromycin base and posaconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 31. Pravastatin: Erythromycin base increases the toxicity of pravastatin by inhibiting OATP1B1 transport. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Prednisolone: Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of prednisolone via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Prednisone: Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of prednisone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Prednisone decreases the level of erythromycin base by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for toxic steroid concentrations and altered mental status. 34. Pretomanid: Pretomanid increases the level or effect of erythromycin base. Both drugs are associated with hepatotoxicity. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 35. Primaquine: Erythromycin base and primaquine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 36. Primidone: Primidone decreases the level or effect of erythromycin base by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 37. Procainamide: Erythromycin base and procainamide both prolong the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. 38. Prochlorperazine: Erythromycin base and prochlorperazine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 39. Promazine: Erythromycin base and promazine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 40. Promethazine: Erythromycin base and promethazine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 41. Propafenone: Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of propafenone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Protriptyline: Erythromycin base and protriptyline both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 43. Pyridoxine: Erythromycin base decreases the level or effect of pyridoxine by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Quetiapine: Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of quetiapine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 45. Quinidine: Erythromycin base and quinidine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 46. Quinine: Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of quinine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Quinupristin/Dalfopristin: This combination increases erythromycin base levels by inhibiting its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 48. Quizartinib: Erythromycin base and quizartinib both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely with frequent ECGs. 49. Rabeprozole: Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of rabeprozole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 50. Ramelteon: Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of ramelteon by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Ranolazine: Erythromycin base and ranolazine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 52. Repaglinide: Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of repaglinide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 53. Repotrectinib: Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of repotrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 54. Resmetirom: Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of resmetirom by inhibiting OATP1B1/3 transport. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 55. Revefenacin: Erythromycin base increases the level of revefenacin by inhibiting OATP1B1/3 transport. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 56. Ribociclib: Ribociclib increases the toxicity of erythromycin base by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 57. Rifabutin: Rifabutin decreases the level of erythromycin base by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Erythromycin base increases the level of rifabutin by inhibiting its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 58. Rifampin: Rifampin decreases the level of erythromycin base by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 59. Rifapentine: Rifapentine decreases the level of erythromycin base by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 60. Rifaximin: Erythromycin base increases the level of rifaximin via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 61. Rilpivirine: Erythromycin base increases the level of rilpivirine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 62. Rimegepant: Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of rimegepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 63. Riociguat: Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of riociguat by inhibiting its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Monitor for signs of hypotension. 64. Risperidone: Erythromycin base increases the level or effect of risperidone via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely.
